# 3-Day Lisbon Budget Trip for 2 Adults

A central, walk-friendly Lisbon plan with **local food**, short transit hops, and a **total target under 900 EUR** for 2 adults, excluding flights.
I’m assuming a mid-range budget stay in Baixa/Chiado or nearby, using public transit and a few taxis only if needed.

## Day-by-Day Lisbon Itinerary and Cost Plan

### Day 1: Baixa, Chiado, Alfama
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/geo-alt.svg
- Morning: Arrive, check in, and start in **Baixa**; walk Praça do Comércio, Rua Augusta, and Rossio.
- Afternoon: Ride or walk up to **Alfama**; visit São Jorge Castle area, Miradouros, and narrow lanes.
- Dinner: Simple local meal in Alfama or Baixa: grilled fish, bifana, or prato do dia.
- Transit tip: Use the **28E tram only if it’s not crowded**; otherwise walk uphill in short segments or use a taxi for the steepest part.

### Day 2: Belém + Riverside
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/water.svg
- Morning: Take tram/train to **Belém**; see Jerónimos exterior, Belém Tower area, and riverside paths.
- Afternoon: Keep it light with **MAAT exterior** or riverside stroll; return to center before rush hour.
- Dinner: Eat in Cais do Sodré or Bairro Alto edge for affordable petiscos and vinho.
- Transit tip: The **train from Cais do Sodré to Belém** is usually easier than the tram and keeps walking manageable.

### Day 3: Time Out Market, Bairro Alto, Viewpoints
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/shop.svg
- Morning: Start at **Time Out Market** or nearby Mercado da Ribeira area for a flexible breakfast/lunch.
Media: Alt=Morning: Start at **Time Out Market** or nearby Mercado da Ribeira area for a flexible breakfast/lunch, Lisbon, Portugal
- Afternoon: Explore **Bairro Alto** and nearby viewpoints; keep the route compact and avoid crisscrossing the city.
- Dinner: Finish with a budget-friendly final meal in Chiado/Baixa, then enjoy a sunset miradouro if energy allows.
- Transit tip: This is your best **mostly-on-foot day**; use the metro only to reset if needed.

## Budget Breakdown for 2 Adults

| Category | Estimated Cost |
|---|---:|
| Central lodging, 3 nights | 390–540 EUR |
| Food and drinks | 180–260 EUR |
| Local transit | 20–40 EUR |
| Attractions and small entries | 40–90 EUR |
| Coffee, snacks, buffer | 60–100 EUR |
| Total estimated trip cost | **690–1,030 EUR** |

### Best budget target to stay under 900 EUR
- Aim for lodging around **430–480 EUR total**
- Keep paid attractions limited to **1–2 per day**
- Use **public transit + walking** instead of taxis
- Choose **daily lunch specials** and simple dinners

## Rainy-Day Backup for Lisbon

### Rain Plan: Covered and Low-Walk Version
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/cloud-rain.svg
- Swap outdoor viewpoints for **Time Out Market**, **Museu Nacional do Azulejo**, and **Carmo Convent area** only if weather improves.
- Spend more time in **Baixa/Chiado** so you can move between stops with short indoor breaks.
- Add a **tram or metro loop** instead of long walks when rain is steady.
- Keep one flexible indoor meal stop near your hotel to reduce backtracking.

## Transit and Walking Tips

- Stay in **Baixa, Chiado, or Cais do Sodré** for the easiest access to most sights.
- Lisbon is hilly, so plan **2–3 main stops per half-day** rather than trying to cover too much.
- Use **metro/train for longer hops**, and save walking for neighborhoods rather than cross-city transfers.
- If you want to reduce fatigue, choose a hotel near a metro stop and a tram line.
